about: The muscles of the jaw, the hyoid, the front and side of the neck and the front of the cervical spine, drawn from their Gray's attachments on the skull, mandible, hyoid, sternum, clavicle, scapula, cervical vertebrae and first two ribs. They are skeletal muscle, so the drives are the whole-body ones the engine has: muscle tone (rigidity and paralysis, including a neuromuscular blocker), a seizure, shivering, swallowing for the hyoid group, and ventilation and respiratory drive for the accessory breathing muscles of the neck. Chewing force, speech, facial expression and neck movement are not simulated, and the muscles of the face are not drawn. The widths of the muscle bellies are drawing choices, not measurements; the attachments are on the model's own bones.

GH14.label: Hall JE, Hall ME. Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th ed. Elsevier, 2021.

GRAYS42.label: Standring S (ed). Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice, 42nd ed. Elsevier, 2020.

parts.label: Muscles of Mastication
parts.summary: The four paired muscles that move the jaw
parts.function: Temporalis, masseter and the medial and lateral pterygoids close, open and slide the jaw. Chewing itself is not simulated.

drives.note: Raised skeletal muscle tone (rigidity) is a rise in the tone of the muscles of the body, so this muscle tightens with it. The weight is a display scale.
Lost skeletal muscle tone (paralysis, or a neuromuscular blocker) lowers the tone of the muscles of the body, so this muscle goes slack. The weight is a display scale.
A seizure is a brief, intense motor discharge, which the engine reports as 0 or 1; skeletal muscle contracts in it. The weight is a display scale.
Shivering is rhythmic contraction of skeletal muscle in the cold, so this muscle is engaged by it. The weight is a display scale.

parts.label: Temporalis
parts.summary: A fan-shaped muscle on the side of the skull
parts.function: It arises from the temporal fossa and gathers onto the coronoid process of the mandible. It closes the jaw and pulls it back.

parts.label: Masseter
parts.summary: The thick muscle over the ramus of the mandible
parts.function: It runs from the zygomatic arch to the angle and ramus of the mandible and closes the jaw.

parts.label: Superficial Part of Masseter
parts.summary: The larger front layer of the masseter
parts.function: It arises from the front of the zygomatic arch and passes down and back to the angle of the mandible.

parts.label: Deep Part of Masseter
parts.summary: The smaller back layer of the masseter
parts.function: It arises from the back and inner surface of the zygomatic arch and passes down to the upper ramus.

parts.label: Lateral Pterygoid
parts.summary: A short muscle deep to the ramus that draws the jaw forward
parts.function: It runs from the sphenoid bone back to the neck of the mandible and the joint disc, and it opens the jaw and moves it from side to side.

parts.label: Upper Head of Lateral Pterygoid
parts.summary: The head from the infratemporal surface of the sphenoid
parts.function: It arises from the greater wing of the sphenoid bone and passes back and out to the neck of the mandible.

parts.label: Lower Head of Lateral Pterygoid
parts.summary: The head from the lateral pterygoid plate
parts.function: It arises from the outer surface of the lateral pterygoid plate and passes back and out to the neck of the mandible.

parts.label: Medial Pterygoid
parts.summary: A muscle on the inner face of the ramus
parts.function: It runs from the pterygoid fossa down and back to the inner surface of the angle of the mandible and helps to close the jaw.

parts.label: Hyoid Muscles
parts.summary: The suprahyoid and infrahyoid muscles around the hyoid bone
parts.function: The suprahyoid muscles join the hyoid to the jaw and skull and the infrahyoid muscles join it to the sternum, clavicle and scapula. They lift and steady the hyoid and the larynx, which is part of the swallow.

drives.note: Swallowing raises the hyoid and the larynx, which these muscles do; the engine's swallowing signal is 1 while something is in the oesophagus.
Raised skeletal muscle tone (rigidity) is a rise in the tone of the muscles of the body, so this muscle tightens with it. The weight is a display scale.
Lost skeletal muscle tone (paralysis, or a neuromuscular blocker) lowers the tone of the muscles of the body, so this muscle goes slack. The weight is a display scale.

parts.label: Digastric
parts.summary: A two-bellied muscle from the mastoid region to the chin
parts.function: Its posterior belly runs from the mastoid notch and its anterior belly to the mandible, joined by an intermediate tendon at the hyoid. It lowers the jaw and raises the hyoid.

parts.label: Posterior Belly of Digastric
parts.summary: The belly from the mastoid notch
parts.function: It runs from the mastoid notch of the temporal bone forward and down to the intermediate tendon.

parts.label: Intermediate Tendon of Digastric
parts.summary: The tendon joining the two bellies
parts.function: It is held to the hyoid bone by a fibrous sling.

parts.label: Anterior Belly of Digastric
parts.summary: The belly to the chin
parts.function: It runs from the intermediate tendon forward and up to the digastric fossa of the mandible beside the midline.

parts.label: Stylohyoid
parts.summary: A slender muscle from the styloid process to the hyoid
parts.function: It runs alongside the posterior belly of the digastric and draws the hyoid up and back.

parts.label: Mylohyoid
parts.summary: The muscular floor of the mouth
parts.function: A sheet from the mylohyoid line of the mandible to a midline raphe and the hyoid body, it raises the floor of the mouth and the hyoid. The mouth organ draws the tongue above it.

parts.label: Geniohyoid
parts.summary: A short muscle above the mylohyoid beside the midline
parts.function: It runs from the inferior mental spine of the mandible to the body of the hyoid and draws the hyoid forward and up.

parts.label: Sternohyoid
parts.summary: An infrahyoid strap from the sternum to the hyoid
parts.function: It runs from the back of the manubrium and the medial clavicle up the front of the neck to the hyoid and pulls the hyoid down.

parts.label: Omohyoid
parts.summary: An infrahyoid muscle with two bellies and a tendon between
parts.function: Its inferior belly arises from the upper border of the scapula and, after an intermediate tendon, its superior belly reaches the hyoid. It steadies and lowers the hyoid.

parts.label: Inferior Belly of Omohyoid
parts.summary: The belly from the scapula
parts.function: It crosses the lower neck from the superior border of the scapula to the intermediate tendon.

parts.label: Intermediate Tendon of Omohyoid
parts.summary: The tendon between the two bellies
parts.function: It is bound down to the clavicle by a sheet of deep fascia.

parts.label: Superior Belly of Omohyoid
parts.summary: The belly to the hyoid
parts.function: It runs up beside the sternohyoid to the lower border of the hyoid.

parts.label: Sternothyroid
parts.summary: A deeper infrahyoid strap to the thyroid cartilage
parts.function: It runs from the back of the manubrium to the oblique line of the thyroid cartilage and pulls the larynx down.

parts.label: Thyrohyoid
parts.summary: The short continuation of the sternothyroid
parts.function: It runs from the thyroid cartilage up to the hyoid and brings the two closer.

parts.label: Sternocleidomastoid
parts.summary: The muscle that runs obliquely across the side of the neck
parts.function: It runs from the sternum and clavicle to the mastoid process of the skull. It turns and tilts the head, and in forced breathing it helps to lift the sternum.

drives.note: Guyton and Hall name this muscle among those that raise the ribs or sternum in a deeper breath, so a rise in minute ventilation engages it. The weight is a display scale.

Guyton and Hall name this muscle among those recruited when breathing is driven harder (accessory inspiration or forced expiration), so a rise in central respiratory drive engages it. The weight is a display scale.

parts.label: Sternal Head of Sternocleidomastoid
parts.summary: The rounded tendon from the manubrium
parts.function: It arises from the front of the manubrium of the sternum.

parts.label: Clavicular Head of Sternocleidomastoid
parts.summary: The broader fleshy part from the clavicle
parts.function: It arises from the upper surface of the medial part of the clavicle and joins the sternal head.

parts.label: Scalene Muscles
parts.summary: The three muscles from the neck vertebrae to the first two ribs
parts.function: They bend the neck, and in a deeper breath they lift the first two ribs.

drives.note: Guyton and Hall name this muscle among those that raise the ribs or sternum in a deeper breath, so a rise in minute ventilation engages it. The weight is a display scale.

parts.label: Anterior Scalene
parts.summary: The front scalene
parts.function: It runs from the cervical transverse processes to the first rib, in front of the subclavian artery.

parts.label: Middle Scalene
parts.summary: The middle and largest scalene
parts.function: It runs from the cervical transverse processes to the first rib behind the subclavian artery.

parts.label: Posterior Scalene
parts.summary: The back scalene
parts.function: It runs from the lower cervical transverse processes to the second rib.

parts.label: Prevertebral Muscles
parts.summary: The muscles on the front of the cervical spine
parts.function: Longus colli and longus capitis flex the neck and head. They lie behind the pharynx.

parts.label: Longus Colli
parts.summary: A muscle on the front of the cervical and upper thoracic vertebrae
parts.function: It lies on the front of the vertebral bodies and flexes the neck. Gray's describes three parts; they are drawn as one strap here.

parts.label: Longus Capitis
parts.summary: A muscle from the cervical vertebrae to the base of the skull
parts.function: It runs from the anterior tubercles of the cervical transverse processes to the underside of the occipital bone and flexes the head.

parts.label: Platysma
parts.summary: A thin sheet in the skin of the neck
parts.function: It spreads from the fascia over the upper chest and shoulder up over the clavicle and the neck to the lower border of the mandible. It tenses the skin of the neck.
